correctness.rationale: The binary greedy-arch scan (store first unseen letter, close at first different letter) has number of complete arches equal to scattered-subsequence universality index iota; any length-iota binary word chooses its symbols arch by arch, while a target of length iota+1 is missing after the incomplete one-letter suffix. For each Dyck prefix define K arches, register L, height H≤h, parity J=K mod2, and R=prefix_length−B(K), B(2q)=2hq+2, B(2q+1)=2h(q+1). The six-case potential Φ(H,L,J) in actual RESULT.md satisfies R≤Φ by direct one-step transition inequalities, using reachable-state restrictions H=h⇒L=0 and H=h−1⇒L≠1. The final state H=0 has Φ≤0, proving semilength n≤h(k+1)/2 for odd k and n≤hk/2+1 for even k. Words (0^h1^h)^q and its appended 01 reach both bounds; partial final mountains prove the stated minimum-index n/h residue formula and height1 alternate case. Independent exhaustive n≤8 Dyck generation, direct target-subsequence tests, and exact greedy-index comparison yielded 2055 word checks and 64 min-pairs; finite tests do not establish arbitrary height, for which the displayed symbolic potential is decisive.
